summary: This work generalizes multiple Andreev reflection (MAR) theory to asymmetric Josephson junctions with unequal superconducting gaps, enabling quantitative interpretation of STM-based Nb–Nb junctions across three transport regimes. By measuring $I$–$V$ characteristics over normal-state resistances $R_n = 1$ kΩ to 10 MΩ at 50 mK and 1.5 K, the authors extract the tip and sample gaps ($\Delta_t \approx 0.67$ meV, $\Delta_s \approx 1.51$ meV), barrier transparency ($D$ ranging from 0.1 to 0.6), and effective channel number ($N = 2$ to 20).
motivation: Josephson STM junctions commonly exhibit gap asymmetry from tip oxidation or preparation-induced variations, yet existing symmetric MAR models fail to reliably extract transport parameters; understanding asymmetric MAR is crucial for interpreting superconducting STM spectroscopy and small-junction physics in qubits.
method: The authors generalized the Averin–Bardas MAR formalism to different gaps at left and right Andreev interfaces, deriving recursion relations for wavefunction amplitudes and the dc current via Eq. (8). They fit voltage- and current-biased $I(V)$ and $dI/dV$ data using a simplified model with $N$ identical channels of transparency $D$, yielding gaps and transport properties; junction dynamics were analyzed using the RCSJ model with capacitance values of order fF.
result: The extracted tip gap decreased $\sim 15\%$ from $R_n = 57$ kΩ to 1 kΩ, indicating pressure or heating effects; switching current was suppressed to 1–10% of the MAR-predicted critical current $I_c$ for $10$ kΩ $< R_n < 100$ kΩ, consistent with phase diffusion; supercurrent branch resistance scaled as $R_z \propto R_n^2$ at both temperatures, agreeing with thermal Nyquist noise theory predicting $Z_1 \sim 800$–1800 Ω.
